variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture is the complete system that finds evidence for a question, places a bounded set of that evidence in a model prompt, and decides whether the resulting answer is safe to release.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Add complexity only for a measured retrieval failure”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Single-query RAG
pairs.detail: Run one bounded query, select evidence, and generate once.
pairs.explanation: Run one bounded query, select evidence, and generate once. Prefer this when questions are direct and the corpus uses consistent terminology.

pairs.label: Hybrid retrieval
pairs.explanation: Combine exact-term and semantic signals. This helps when identifiers need lexical precision while paraphrases need vector recall.

pairs.label: Hierarchical retrieval
pairs.detail: Route through document or section summaries, then retrieve detailed passages from the selected parents.
pairs.explanation: Route through document or section summaries, then retrieve detailed passages from the selected parents. Use it when document structure carries meaning.

pairs.label: Multi-query retrieval
pairs.detail: Decompose a question into bounded subqueries and merge evidence.
pairs.explanation: Decompose a question into bounded subqueries and merge evidence. Use it only when one query repeatedly misses required facts.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is no evidence, no grounded claim.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Single-query RAG: Run one bounded query, select evidence, and generate once. Hybrid retrieval: Combine exact-term and semantic signals. Hierarchical retrieval: Route through document or section summaries, then retrieve detailed passages from the selected parents. Multi-query retrieval: Decompose a question into bounded subqueries and merge evidence.

pairs.label: Apply hard filters

pairs.label: Retrieve for recall
pairs.detail: Use lexical search for exact identifiers, vectors for semantic similarity, or both when the workload contains both query shapes.

pairs.label: Rerank for precision
pairs.detail: Spend the expensive relevance model on a bounded candidate pool, then remove duplicates and passages that do not add a required fact.

pairs.detail: Reserve answer and instruction tokens, order evidence deliberately, and retain source-to-passage mappings for citations.

variants.context: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture is the complete system that finds evidence for a question, places a bounded set of that evidence in a model prompt, and decides whether the resulting answer is safe to release.
variants.prompt: What is the core grounding invariant for a RAG answer?
options: No evidence, no grounded claim.
Every query must use agentic retrieval.
A large context window guarantees correctness.
A model confidence score replaces source citations.
variants.explanation: The answer service should make material claims only when selected, authorized evidence supports them; otherwise it should refuse or state what is missing.

variants.prompt: Why should retrieval and generation be evaluated separately?
options: So the model can choose its own access policy.
To distinguish missing or bad evidence from failure to use good evidence.
Because end-to-end answer quality is never useful.
To avoid recording source versions.
variants.explanation: Separate measurements localize the fault: retrieval may miss the source, or generation may ignore and miscite a good evidence packet.

variants.prompt: A selected evidence packet contains an old policy that conflicts with the current approved source. What is the correct release behavior?

Ask the model to average the policies.
Block or resolve the conflict under a freshness policy before answering.
Hide both citations and answer confidently.
variants.explanation: Similarity does not establish authority or effective time. Conflicting or stale evidence must be filtered or resolved before release.
